entries.lead: See what is left on an API key.
entries.detail: DeepSeek and Kimi connections show their prepaid balance, such as `¥2.90 left`, and a MiniMax plan key shows its five-hour and weekly windows: beside the connection in **Settings > Agents > API keys**, on a meter of its own at the foot of the rail, and in the Inbox's plan. The meter measures a balance against your last top-up and turns amber and then red as it runs low; turn it off in **Settings > Appearance > Usage meters**.

entries.lead: See what's new in Nodex without leaving the app.
entries.detail: **Feedback & community** in the account menu now opens on the three newest releases, each with its headline and date, and a filled dot marks the ones released since you last looked. Choose one to read its release notes in place, or open the full changelog on the website.

entries.lead: Arrange the sidebar by attention.
entries.detail: Turn on the toggle beside Search (`⌥⌘U`) to list **Pinned** chats, then **Active** chats waiting on you, **Working** chats whose Agents are busy and **Snoozed** chats, and **View options** beside the first list chooses which lists show and whether they cover every Project or just one. Each row names its Project and previews what came back, and a chat whose Page waits on you says so first, such as **Ready for your review**. Rows hold still while you point at the sidebar, `⌥⌘↑` and `⌥⌘↓` move between chats, and `⌥⌘A` jumps to the next one that needs you.

entries.lead: Settle a chat when you’re finished with it.
entries.detail: The check on its row, its menu or `⌥⌘E` moves it to the Settled shelf and opens the next chat, and Undo puts it back. **Settle read chats** clears the rest of the read ones at once. A settled chat reopens when you write to it or its Agent needs you; chats also settle after the idle days you choose and when their Page’s work is Done, and on a chat waiting for your review the check reads **Accept and settle**.

entries.lead: Snooze a chat from the clock on its row or `⌥⌘Z`, until a preset time or one you pick.
entries.detail: A snooze can hold a question or an approval until later, and its Inbox item returns at the same time; a new request brings the chat back sooner, and a chat whose snooze ends says **Back from snooze**.

entries.lead: API keys now run on Nodex's built-in Codex.
entries.detail: Codex talks to the provider's OpenAI Responses API and knows each model's context window and reasoning levels, such as DeepSeek's Low, High and Max, and connecting a key no longer downloads Claude Code. Choose **Runs on: Claude Code** when connecting to keep using Claude Code, or for an endpoint that only serves the Anthropic Messages API; keys you already connected keep running on Claude Code with their chats.

entries.lead: Nodex's model guide now covers GPT-6.2 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Neon, each judged on its own.
entries.detail: Inbox suggestions send backend and systems work to GPT-6.2 Sol and can give UI work to Gemini 4 Neon when the Claude budget runs low. GPT-6.1 models and OpenCode's free models no longer carry a guide note, so the Inbox's plan no longer marks free models `Free`.

entries.lead: Automations that react to GitHub events no longer take a schedule.
entries.detail: Each Automation now has one `trigger`: a clock with an RRULE and timezone, or GitHub events, which has no RRULE, timezone or next run. Agents and `nodex automations create|update` put the schedule or event filter under `trigger`, and the old top-level `rrule`, `timezone` and `source_condition` fields are refused instead of silently replaced.

entries.lead: File search finds files from loose abbreviations.
entries.detail: Type the letters of a name in order, like `fileindxmod` for `file-index-module.ts`, or several words such as `palette test`, and the matches come up with the matched letters highlighted. A file named exactly what you typed comes first. `'` matches exact text, `^` and `$` anchor to the start or end of the path, and `!` leaves matches out. Search on this computer and on remote computers now ranks the same way.

entries.lead: **Remind me** on chats and **Later** in the Inbox are now one **Snooze**.
entries.detail: **Wake** ends a chat’s snooze early, the Inbox’s **Snoozed** view lists items by when they’ll return, and pinning a chat lives in its menu.

entries.lead: Antigravity and other ACP chats that can resume now pick up your installed plugins on a later reply if they opened before Nodex finished reading them.
An API key connection's chats, assignments, Inbox lines and usage show the provider's own mark instead of Claude Code's.
Chats started with Claude Code get generated titles again.
entries.detail: Nodex titles them with Claude Code's own settings for reaching the model, such as a proxy in its `env`, so a Claude Code that connects through one no longer leaves new chats named after the first 120 characters of their prompt. If the chat's Agent still cannot write a title, another available Agent writes it.

entries.lead: Titles and Git drafts written with a Codex that uses its own model provider now go to that provider.
entries.detail: They used to ignore the provider, endpoint and sign-in settings in Codex's `config.toml` and fall back to OpenAI.

entries.lead: File search no longer shows matches and then replaces them with "File search is unavailable".
entries.detail: Matches stay put, and when a folder can't be searched completely, a line below the results says why: the folder is too large, no longer exists, or Nodex isn't allowed to read it. If search itself stops, select **Couldn’t search files** to try again. A linked folder that points back inside the same folder is now searched only at its real location, so files your ignore rules hide no longer flood the results through the link.

entries.lead: A subagent that received a follow-up now appears once in the Subagents tab.
entries.detail: Before, each follow-up added another row, the map kept showing the finished first turn while the follow-up was still running, and counts such as "4/5 back" counted turns instead of subagents. The subagent's row and card now show the turn it is working on and keep their place, and Stop stops that turn. The chat's Subagents summary and the Composer's agent mentions list it once too.

entries.lead: A subagent's result arrives once its work is done.
entries.detail: A follow-up that delegated more work no longer reports back before that work finishes, a result no longer waits for a follow-up queued behind it, and a subagent woken by its own subagents' results reports the answer it gave after reading them.

entries.lead: Stopping a subagent now stops all of it.
entries.detail: Its running turn ends, follow-ups waiting behind it never run, and none of them reports back to the Agent that delegated it, while turns that already finished keep their results. A follow-up held after you stop a subagent's own chat no longer keeps the parent chat looking busy, and a message steered into a turn that was just starting no longer reports a separate, cancelled task.

entries.lead: Agent replies keep showing completed paragraphs when the Agent pauses mid-response.
Sessions an Agent starts in a new worktree on a named branch now start instead of failing with `Worktree worker host message violates protocol version 9`.
entries.detail: Saying whether a missing branch should be created or reported no longer breaks workspace preparation.

entries.lead: Pausing or resuming an Automation that reacts to GitHub events keeps it reacting to GitHub events.
entries.detail: It used to lose its event filter and turn into a daily schedule.

entries.lead: Menus, pickers and previews no longer act on what sits behind them.
entries.detail: Dragging inside a List row's Priority or Status picker no longer moves the Page, Undo pressed in a Page's Linked chats no longer reverses a Database edit, closing a Readback's image preview no longer opens its chat, and right-clicking in the Page link picker no longer opens the editor's menu.

entries.lead: Pinned chats reorder when you drag them, in **Pinned** and in each Project's pinned group.
entries.detail: Chats running on Claude Code or another ACP Agent, and drafts, used to ignore the drag or snap back; now every pinned chat keeps the place you drop it in, and pins in other lists stay put.

entries.lead: On Windows, Nodex finds Claude Code conversations in your Windows user profile even when your shell sets a different home directory.
entries.detail: Import and Insights also recognize Claude configuration paths written with Windows home-relative separators.

entries.lead: Local plugin servers that need the Windows system directory can now start in Nodex, so their tools and plugin apps are available.

releases.headline: Plugin tools for Claude Code and ACP

entries.lead: Claude Code chats can use your plugins' MCP tools.
entries.detail: Each plugin server turned Claude Code away with "Invalid lease" as it connected, because Claude Code checks a server before it initializes and Nodex tied the credential to that first check. Plugin servers now accept the chat's credential on every request until the plugin changes or the chat closes.

entries.lead: Antigravity chats open again.
entries.detail: Every message to Antigravity failed with "Nodex application authority is unavailable for this request" while Nodex prepared its plugins. Antigravity now receives your installed plugins' skills and MCP servers like Claude Code and other ACP Agents, and an Agent that hits a problem Nodex can name now shows that problem instead of the same generic message.

entries.lead: ACP Agents that do not announce HTTP MCP support now get your plugins' MCP servers.
entries.detail: They used to receive only the plugins' skills, so tools such as a plugin's local command server were missing from their chats; Nodex now connects those servers the same way it connects its own tools.

entries.lead: Plugins no longer stop you from sending messages to Claude Code or ACP Agents.
entries.detail: Opening several chats at once, or Codex being slow to list your installed plugins, could fail a reply with "Timed out preparing the Session's plugins" until you refreshed the Plugins page. Nodex now keeps the plugins it last read and rereads them in the background, so a reply waits at most a few seconds and starts with the plugins it has, picking up the rest at a later reply. Chats with the same plugins now share one prepared copy of their skills instead of each copying all of them, and a plugin's skills or servers that cannot be prepared are left out without holding up the rest.

releases.headline: Google Antigravity and a smaller Nodex

entries.lead: See the pages an Agent's web search found.
entries.detail: Open a search in a chat to get its results as chips with each site's icon and page title; a chip opens the page. Codex and Claude searches both show their pages, live and when you come back to a chat.

entries.lead: Google Antigravity is a built-in Agent with its own section in **Settings > Agents**.
entries.detail: It starts with a profile that uses the account `agy` is signed in to on your computer, so an `agy` you already use works with no setup. Add a profile for each other account and sign in with Google or connect a Gemini API key, Gemini Enterprise or Agent Platform. Nodex downloads and updates the Antigravity runtime for you, or runs the `agy` you point it at. Chats use the models on your plan with each model's thinking levels, list what Antigravity's subagents did, and its limits sit beside your other usage meters.

entries.lead: Antigravity conversations, from the Antigravity app or its `agy` command line, can be imported from **Settings > Import** beside Codex and Claude Code.
entries.detail: They appear in the same list across every folder, with search, filters and batch import. Each import is a new chat that already shows the full history, including thoughts, commands, file edits and tool calls, and continues as your Antigravity profile. The original conversation stays unchanged.

entries.lead: Choose which large parts of Nodex stay on your Mac.
entries.detail: **Settings > General > Add-ons** lists the parts that install after the app, with a switch to remove each one and get its space back: Desktop Tools (the Browser, your Chrome tabs and Computer Use for Agents), Codex, Claude Code (for Claude with an API key or Nodex credits) and Document Tools (Word, PowerPoint, Excel and PDF files for Agents).

entries.lead: Run your own Codex.
entries.detail: **Settings > Agents > Codex > Codex executable** takes a command or path, and Nodex runs that Codex instead of its own. Nodex shows its version and warns when it differs from the one Nodex is tested with; Desktop Tools stay off in Codex chats while you use it.

entries.lead: The Subagents tab opens on a map of how a chat's work was delegated.
entries.detail: The lead sits on one side and each subagent is a card naming its Agent, model and effort. Each edge takes the color of the harness the work went to and shows whether that work is under way, waiting on you, or back. Subagents that delegate further appear beneath their own card, at any depth. A switch at the top returns to the list.

entries.lead: Decide whether subagents can hand work to more Agents.
entries.detail: **Settings > Chats > Let subagents delegate** sets it for every chat, and the Subagents tab can answer differently for one chat. When it is off, only the Agent you talk to delegates or starts new chats; you can also just ask that Agent to keep a task to itself. Subagents now work on their own task first and delegate only when the task calls for it.

entries.lead: Your agents work together from the first chat.
entries.detail: When setup finds two different agents ready, such as Codex and Claude Code, it says so, and the first task asks one to bring in the other by name: they study your project independently and compare notes, or one builds and the other reviews. You watch the second agent at work in the same chat. Asking for an agent by name works in any chat afterwards.

entries.lead: Nodex introduces things as you meet them.
entries.detail: The first time an agent writes a Page, another agent could give a second opinion, or you start a chat while one is still working, one quiet sentence above the Composer says what it is and offers a way to try it, such as `Ask Claude Code` or `Open Inbox`. Each tip appears once and leaves when you act on it, dismiss it or send your next message. **Settings > General > Show tips** turns them off.

entries.lead: Reach the people who make Nodex from inside the app.
entries.detail: **Feedback & community** in the account menu at the bottom of the rail opens the Nodex Discord server, or copies the number of the Nodex QQ group so you can find it in QQ. Bring bug reports, ideas and questions.

entries.lead: Codex replies that OpenAI's safeguards hide or block after they stream now stay hidden.
entries.detail: Nodex shows a short notice in their place, on your phone too, and other Agents reading the chat see the notice instead of the reply. A reply shown with a support note keeps that note beneath it.

entries.lead: Settings is easier to find your way around.
entries.detail: The sidebar now groups pages by what they are about — the App, your Agents, Integrations, Coding and Data — and every page says what it controls. **Chats** gathers what chats may do without asking, your instructions and how chats look; **Editor** gathers typing, pasting and links; Hooks moved into **Plugins** and Environments into **Worktrees**. **Spaces** is now **Remote**, where you link your phone, invite people and join other computers, and Link a device turns remote connections on for you. Conversations is now **Import**, and Data controls is **Archived chats**.

entries.lead: Each Agent's models are now in its own card in **Settings > Agents**, beside how it signs in, with Nodex's credit-spending models first.
entries.detail: A filter at the top finds any model across them. Only Nodex keeps a switch for all of its models; turn another Agent or profile off to turn all of it off.

entries.lead: Branches Nodex creates for chats now start with `nodex/` instead of `codex/`.
entries.detail: A prefix you set in **Settings > Git** stays as it is.

entries.lead: A busy computer no longer puts "Agent execution isn't responding" on every window.
entries.detail: Running many Agents, builds and tests at once now only slows Agent execution, and a chat that is still opening says your computer is busy and opens when Nodex catches up. The notice and its Restart appear only when Agent execution has made no progress for a minute. Opening a chat also goes ahead of background work and no longer waits while other Agents save their progress.

entries.lead: Nodex uses less memory and CPU while Agents work.
entries.detail: When a chat changes, search now rereads only that chat instead of every chat, which on a Profile with thousands of chats removes about a gigabyte of short-lived memory a minute. Nodex's processes also hold about 75 MB less code and data for as long as they run, and a minimized or covered window stops redrawing until you show it.

entries.lead: Typing no longer waits on your disk.
entries.detail: Drafts and other window state used to be rewritten and synced to disk with every keystroke, so a disk kept busy by builds and tests could hold up every window; they are now saved in the background, with changes made meanwhile saved together.

entries.lead: Opening many Pages no longer keeps them all in memory.
entries.detail: A window keeps the four Pages you viewed most recently ready to show, and a Page older than that loads again when you return to its tab, with its undo history starting fresh.

entries.lead: A New tab is now a calm launcher:
entries.detail: a search field for Pages, tools and websites, then the tools you pinned under Open. Pin, unpin and reorder tools from Open's … menu or with Customize, and every New tab in that panel follows your choice. Browser controls appear once the tab loads a site.

entries.lead: Setup lists the Agents that are ready first, then the ones already on your computer that need one more step, then the rest.
entries.detail: A row keeps its place once it has one.

entries.lead: Antigravity has one place in Nodex:
entries.detail: **Settings > Agents > Antigravity**. An Antigravity you connected under **Other agents** becomes its profile that uses `agy`'s sign-in on your computer, and its chats continue there once you choose an Antigravity model. Searching the ACP Registry for Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode now leads to the built-in Agent instead of adding a second copy.

entries.lead: Nodex for Mac is less than a third of its size:
entries.detail: the installer drops from about 600 MB to 180 MB and the app from 2.1 GB to 0.64 GB. Desktop Tools download in the background after Nodex starts and work as soon as they arrive, with no restart. Codex, Claude Code and Document Tools download the first time you use them; if you already use Codex in Nodex, it comes back by itself after you update. Updates are less than a third of the size too, and bring a new version of a part only when that part changed, fetching it before you restart.

entries.lead: Nodex opens and works without Codex.
entries.detail: Pages, search, Git and every other Agent no longer depend on it, so a missing or damaged Codex no longer stops the app from starting.

entries.lead: Streaming replies and long chats take far less work.
entries.detail: While a long answer streams, Nodex's processes exchange about 17 times less data, and about 90 times less during a long thought: a reply's text travels between them once instead of with every update, and nothing is re-sent when it has not changed. Each update touches only its own message, and a long chat keeps only the messages near what you are reading on screen.

entries.lead: Chats no longer keep their JavaScript processes running after you stop using them.
entries.detail: A chat's JavaScript session now closes after 30 minutes without use and starts fresh with its next JavaScript call, so a Nodex left running no longer collects a set of background processes for every chat that ran JavaScript.

entries.lead: Nodex opens with much less code in the way.
entries.detail: Its window appears once about 1.4 MB of the app has loaded instead of 9.9 MB, with the rest loading behind it, and each window loads about 8 MB less: Pages, Databases, the Browser, the drawing canvas, the Terminal, the code highlighter and other surfaces load only when you open them, and error reporting only when it is on.

entries.lead: Returning to a chat you just left shows it at once.
entries.detail: Each window keeps the three chats it most recently showed up to date for a minute, so switching back reads nothing again, and opening a chat now takes half the requests it did.

entries.lead: Code in chats and documents no longer slows the window while it is colored.
entries.detail: Its text appears at once and is colored in the background as it scrolls into view; while a reply streams a code block, the part already colored keeps its colors as new lines arrive.

entries.lead: Nodex opens straight onto your first view.
entries.detail: The window used to step from the Nodex mark to a blank window, then to a sidebar beside an empty pane, before the view appeared; now the mark stays until the view is ready and dissolves into it in one step, or swaps at once with Reduce motion.

entries.lead: Process Manager no longer weighs on the app while it is open.
entries.detail: Each refresh reads every process once, away from the windows' main work, however many chats have background processes, and CPU now shows the share used since the previous refresh.

entries.lead: Searching chats no longer holds up the rest of Nodex.
entries.detail: Results are ranked in the background, so typing in Find stays smooth while replies stream, and an idle Nodex no longer rereads every Codex chat each second: it refreshes only the chats that changed or whose host reconnected.

entries.lead: One Writing model writes chat titles, commit messages and pull request descriptions.
entries.detail: Choose it in **Settings > Chats**; it replaces the chat title model, and any Agent can do the writing. When your choice is unavailable, Nodex uses the Agent of the chat you are in, then another available Agent.

entries.lead: Setup's first task reads in plain words and in your display language.
entries.detail: It no longer asks for a "Nodex Page" before you have seen one.

entries.lead: An Agent's work in a chat reads as one live line.
entries.detail: While it works, the line names the tool that is running, and each new tool's words wipe in as the last ones fade, without cutting in mid-shimmer. Its icon animates while the tool runs and holds still between tools. Opened, the steps hang from a thin line at their full length instead of scrolling in a short box: each command shows the command itself, each edit its file and line counts.

entries.lead: Searching a Page no longer takes over your cursor.
entries.detail: After `Cmd/Ctrl+F` or opening a Page from a search result, the matched words used to stay selected, so clicking elsewhere and typing could jump back and replace them. Find now only highlights matches: you can click and type anywhere while it stays open, and its highlights follow your edits without scrolling the Page. Pressing Escape hands the current match to the Page as your selection.

entries.lead: Menus keep up with the pointer.
entries.detail: Moving across the rows of a menu opened from a Page, Inbox item or other panel tab used to stall each highlight for a moment, because every row the pointer crossed made the whole window redraw. Rows now highlight as soon as the pointer reaches them, and hovering a menu no longer adds Back steps or clears Forward.

entries.lead: Clicking the group beside a Project's or Inbox's Home tab makes that group active.
entries.detail: It used to switch straight back to Home's group.

entries.lead: Claude Agent can use Nodex's tools again.
entries.detail: Its current releases ask for them in a form Nodex did not answer, so Nodex's own tools, such as Pages and Desktop Tools, were missing from its chats. Nodex now hands its tools to Claude Agent the way it does to every other ACP Agent.

entries.lead: Claude Agent chats offer Claude's slash commands as soon as they open, and its work no longer lists "Unsupported ACP update" steps.
entries.detail: Nodex now speaks the current Agent Client Protocol, so commands an Agent lists when a chat starts reach the `/` menu and its newer updates are understood.

entries.lead: Drafting a commit message or pull request description works again.
entries.detail: The draft buttons in **Commit or push** and **Create pull request** failed on every attempt.

entries.lead: A chat waiting on a long delegated task no longer shows as stalled in the Inbox.
entries.detail: Nodex used to count only the chat's own messages as progress, so a chat that handed work to another Agent for more than twenty minutes was marked "Stalled · needs you" while that Agent was still working. Progress anywhere in the delegated work now counts.

entries.lead: A signed-in Codex no longer shows as "Isn't ready" with nothing to do.
entries.detail: Setup, the Composer and the model menu now say what happened: signed in but unable to connect, not answering in time, or unable to start, each with Check again. Nodex reads Codex's sign-in from your computer before it asks the network, so being offline never hides your account. Codex is ready in about a second instead of about nine, and turns ready by itself when the connection returns.

entries.lead: Agents installed on your computer are found however Nodex was opened.
entries.detail: Claude Code, OpenCode and Google Antigravity are found when Nodex starts from the Dock or Finder, even if your shell's startup files are slow or fail, and an older copy earlier on your PATH no longer hides a working one. A version too old to connect is shown with the version it needs, in setup and in Settings → Agents.

entries.lead: The command palette opens on the search field, with its scope tabs at the bottom next to each scope's options:
entries.detail: Everywhere or one Project, a folder, or file types. Each result is one line, with the title on the left and its Project on the right. A second line appears only to show why it matched. A spinner in the corner shows while a search is still running.

entries.lead: Nodex starts and upgrades normally after a chat continues work that it previously reported ready for review.
Chat search and heartbeats recover when an action is canceled during Agent startup.
Space content loads when a window opens during startup, without needing a reload.
A message that did not go through from your phone stays in the chat.
entries.detail: It used to vanish behind a brief notice, and sending it again could deliver it twice. It now shows that it is sending, waits out a short gap in the connection, and if it could not be sent says why and offers Retry and Delete; Retry never delivers the same message twice. Starting a new chat again after a lost connection opens the same chat instead of a second one.

entries.lead: Stop on your phone stops the Run you are looking at.
entries.detail: If that Run finished a moment earlier, Stop no longer reports a failure or reaches the next Run.

entries.lead: `/compact`, `/goal` and signing out sent while an Agent is working wait for their own turn instead of failing.
Starting a chat from your phone while work is paused asks you to resume work, instead of reporting that the request could not be completed.
Run GPT-6.2 Sol at Ultrafast.
entries.detail: Hover the speed button in the model picker to choose Standard, Fast or Ultrafast, each with what it costs; the button shows the speed in force, and `/ultrafast` switches it from the composer. Only the speeds a model offers are listed, and **Settings > Agents > Codex > Speed** can make Ultrafast the default for new chats. A chat whose model lacks the speed you carried over runs at the next speed down instead of failing.

entries.lead: Start a skill by typing `/` in the Composer.
entries.detail: Your skills appear under **Skills** after the chat's commands, each showing where it comes from and which plugin supplies it; type part of a name to narrow the list and press Enter to put the skill in your message. Commands and skills now match the way `@` does, with the matched letters highlighted.

entries.lead: New Codex chats start on GPT-6.2 Astra, and Inbox suggestions run on GPT-6.2 Sol.
entries.detail: GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol stay available in the model picker.

entries.lead: Choosing a model, reasoning level, project or fork from `/` now works like the rest of the menu.
entries.detail: The choices open in place, you can type to narrow them (spaces included) and pick with the arrow keys and Enter, the current setting is checked, and Backspace takes you back. Model and Reasoning list exactly what the model picker offers, for every Agent, and apply the same way.

entries.lead: Claude Code's `/` menu shows only commands that work in a chat, under **Claude Code**.
entries.detail: Commands for its terminal display, internal handoffs and ones Nodex already offers, such as `/model`, `/effort`, `/usage` or `/clear`, no longer appear twice or do nothing; Nodex's own version is listed instead. Feedback opens its own dialog.

entries.lead: Search finds the text you can see.
entries.detail: Typing part of a Page or chat now finds it wherever that text sits: a Chinese word in the middle of a sentence, one part of `local-first`, `page_search.rs` or `PageSearchKernel`, another form of a word (`migrate` finds `migration`), a small typo, or full-width text typed in half-width. Close matches are listed after exact ones. The same query finds the same things in the command palette, `@` mentions, Database View search, Relation pickers, the Browser address bar, the Agent’s `search` tool, and `nodex search`. Attachment names, link addresses, mentioned Page titles and Property names are searchable too. Database View search reaches every eligible Page in the Data Source, including Pages you haven’t scrolled to, and keeps the View’s filters, sorting and groups.

entries.lead: Choosing a search result opens it where it matched.
entries.detail: A Page opens scrolled to the matching Block and a chat to the matching message, with Find already on the matched text so Enter steps through the other occurrences.

entries.lead: Chat search no longer misses older or scattered matches.
entries.detail: A chat is found when the words you type are spread across its title and several messages, commands the Agent ran and files it changed are searchable, and a strong match in an old chat is no longer hidden behind weaker recent ones. Native Codex chats use the same matching and open at the selected message. History joins in the background, including readable remote hosts; search says when history is still catching up or more matches exist than it shows.

entries.lead: Find Pages and chats across the Space, including archived results.
entries.detail: The palette can narrow search to one Project and highlights a strong Top result in All. Agents can search Pages, Blocks, and chats with the same tool.

entries.lead: Find uses one bar for Pages, chats, diffs and the Browser.
entries.detail: It ignores accents and character width, finds text across inline formatting, and offers Replace in writable Pages. `Cmd/Ctrl+G` and `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G` move to the next and previous match; chat search remains in the command palette and `O T`.

entries.lead: Searching a Database View finds every matching row, not only the rows already loaded.
entries.detail: The View keeps its own filters, sort and groups, and Agents reading the View you see get the same rows.

entries.lead: Pasting a Page link on an empty line inserts a mention instead of embedding the whole Page.
entries.detail: To embed it, right-click the mention and choose **Turn into embed**; the same menu opens the Page or copies its deeplink.

entries.lead: The command palette's Page Filter.
entries.detail: Narrow a search to one Project with the place control beside the search field, and filter by Status, Priority, Tags or Assignee in a Database View.

entries.lead: Turning a Page embed into Text, a heading or a list keeps the Page as a mention.
entries.detail: It used to leave an empty line and lose the connection.

entries.lead: A message sent while a chat is still starting is no longer rejected.
entries.detail: Sending from your phone in the moments after a chat began, before the Agent was at work, failed with "Your message wasn't sent"; it now waits and joins the Agent's turn as soon as that turn begins. A message sent while the Agent compacts its context waits as the next message instead of failing.

releases.headline: Simplified Chinese and your own API keys

entries.lead: Use Nodex in Simplified Chinese.
entries.detail: **Settings > General > Language** follows your system language by default, or you can choose English or 简体中文. Open windows and menus switch at once, without a restart, and dialogs and notifications follow. Your Pages, chats and Agent replies stay in the language they were written in.

entries.lead: Use DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM or MiniMax with your own API key.
entries.detail: Paste a key in setup or **Settings > Agents > API keys** and Nodex checks it, lists the provider's models and runs them on its built-in Claude Code, so there is nothing to install. Any other Anthropic-compatible endpoint, such as your team's gateway, works too. Keys are stored encrypted with your system keychain and are never shown again.

entries.lead: Nodex finds Google Antigravity on your computer and connects it in one click.
entries.detail: If Antigravity's `agy` command line is installed, setup and **Settings > Agents > Other agents** offer it with its version, and connecting it keeps your existing Google sign-in and models.

entries.lead: Nodex waits for a chat and its delegated work to finish before offering Accept.
entries.detail: Only the chat's root Agent can report the Page ready, and a later round reopens the work unless you have since changed its Status.

entries.lead: Chats with agents added through the Agent Client Protocol get a real title.
entries.detail: They used to keep their whole opening prompt as the title; Nodex now uses the name the agent gives its own session, unless you chose a title model in Settings or renamed the chat first.

entries.lead: Google Antigravity can answer in Nodex.
entries.detail: Every message to it used to fail before it could start, because it couldn’t read the format of one of Nodex’s tools; Nodex now describes its tools in a form every Agent accepts.

entries.lead: Send a Browser annotation straight to the Agent.
entries.detail: In the annotation editor, ⌘↵ sends the note as its own message, steering a working Agent or queueing as a typed message would, and leaves what you were typing in the chat alone; **Quick annotate** in a page's context menu sends on Enter. The Browser toolbar sends every saved annotation at once, ⌘⇧. turns annotating on and off, and holding Space lets you use the page without leaving it.

entries.lead: Browser annotations stay on the page until they reach the Agent.
entries.detail: A saved annotation used to leave nothing behind but a small tag in the chat, and was lost if its screenshot failed or the Browser had no chat beside it. Each one is now a numbered pin you can reopen, edit or remove; it is kept when you leave annotating, switch tabs or lose the screenshot; and a Project's Browser sends to its Agent Dock. Pins follow text, elements inside frames and scrolling areas, and the Agent is told exactly what each one points at.

entries.lead: Updating a plugin outside Nodex no longer blocks Claude Code or ACP replies.
entries.detail: Nodex reloads the installed plugin before the next reply.

entries.lead: A terminal or background helper that loses its connection no longer leaves Nodex in a broken state, which happened most often on Windows.
entries.detail: The affected terminal or operation now ends cleanly, and you can start it again without restarting Nodex.

entries.lead: Plugins work in every Agent chat.
entries.detail: A plugin installed in Customize → Plugins reaches Codex natively, and Nodex brings its skills and the MCP servers it can run to Claude Code and ACP Agents. Limit a plugin to chosen Projects from its page; servers that need a sign-in, connected apps and hooks stay in Codex, and the plugin's page says so.

entries.lead: Add a plugin from any folder.
entries.detail: Customize → Plugins → Add → Plugin from folder shows what the folder contains before installing it, and Update from folder picks up later changes.

entries.lead: Open plugin apps from the navigation rail, beside a chat, or in a read-only viewer for supported workspace files.
Read and edit the instructions Agents receive in **Settings > Agents**.
entries.detail: **Full Nodex instructions** shows the guidance every chat gets, and **Your instructions** lets you add standing instructions for all of your chats. **Artifact opening** chooses whether Agents open artifacts beside the chat on their own, ask first, or never.

entries.lead: Type `@Nodex` to turn the block you are writing into a Prompt for Nodex.
entries.detail: The `@` menu offers Nodex first, and the block keeps its text and child blocks, so `⌘↵` sends it to the chat beside the Page.

entries.lead: Choose whether a new chat from your Inbox works in a worktree.
entries.detail: **New chats use a worktree** in Inbox settings sets the default, and the dispatch editor shows **Worktree** or **Local** beside the chat's Agent so each message can choose its own. A chat that runs in your checkout stays linked to its message's Page.

entries.lead: Set anything in your Inbox aside with **Later** when it can wait.
entries.detail: Choose a time and the message or the work waiting on you leaves your Inbox, then comes back with a notification when that time arrives; if it needs you for a new reason before then, it shows at once. The new Later view lists everything you set aside in the order it returns, and Nodex can suggest Later for a message that says when the work should wait until. It works on the phone too.

entries.lead: Share to Nodex from other apps on your phone.
entries.detail: Nodex now appears when you share a photo, a link, a web page or text on iPhone and Android, and what you share opens in your Inbox Composer, ready to send or to add a note to first. On iPhone, the share sheet also offers **Add to Nodex Inbox** among its actions.

entries.lead: Choose how hard a model reasons from your phone.
entries.detail: The Agent chip in Nodex Mobile's Composer now names the model and its reasoning effort, and its sheet lists the efforts that model offers, for a new chat or one started from an Inbox message. In an open chat the Composer shows the effort in force and changes it from your next message on.

entries.lead: Save a thought that asks for no work with **Save to Notes**.
entries.detail: Each Project, and the Inbox itself, gets a Notes page; a saved message becomes a page beneath it, off the Board, where you can arrange notes into sections. Nodex suggests it for references and can file a note under a section you already have.

entries.lead: Agents can set properties on many Pages in one step.
entries.detail: Ask a chat to mark a batch of cards Done or re-prioritize a Board and it commits the whole change together and reports each card's resulting values, instead of editing cards one at a time. On the command line, `nodex page properties set NODEX-4 NODEX-8 --set Status=done --set Priority=p1-high` does the same, `nodex page create` takes `--set`, and `nodex page move` moves several Pages at once.

entries.lead: Agents running locally on Windows can use Nodex’s in-app Browser, with the same site access approvals as on macOS.
Computer Use can control desktop apps on Windows.
entries.detail: Manage availability and saved app approvals in Computer use settings.

entries.lead: A Page's toolbar now holds the tools for writing it.
entries.detail: **Text style**, **Image**, **Table**, and **Insert** sit beside the Page's menu and act where your caret is, and **Insert** lists every Block with a short description. The Page menu gathers Rename, Copy, **Download as Markdown**, **Open on right**, and **Open in new window** with the Page's view options, and **Copy link** has its own button.

entries.lead: Start an empty Page from a shape.
entries.detail: A new Page offers **Task brief**, **Bug report**, **To-do list**, and **Meeting notes** under its first line; choosing one writes its headings and puts your caret where to begin.

entries.lead: Alerts and confirmations from a web page now appear inside its Browser tab.
entries.detail: They name the site that asked, leave the rest of Nodex usable, and stop taking the keyboard from the chat you are typing in. A page that keeps opening them can be told to stop, and an Agent working in the page answers them itself.

entries.lead: A message you send from your phone while an Agent is working now redirects it right away, as sending from the desktop does.
entries.detail: Nodex Mobile used to queue it behind the Run unless you knew to press and hold send; now holding send is what queues it, and the Composer says so.

entries.lead: The Inbox and the Board now agree about every message.
entries.detail: A message waits in your Inbox while its card is in Triage and yours to decide, so moving the card on the Board handles it, and moving it back to Triage brings it back. **Keep** is now **Add to Todo**, and a card appears in the Inbox once, whether it waits to be routed or needs your answer or review. In a shared Space, each person's Inbox shows the messages they own.

entries.lead: Stable updates reach you sooner with the same build already tested on Nightly.
entries.detail: Both channels show app versions as `x.y.z`, and you can choose your channel in Settings.

entries.lead: Opening `N more properties` on a Page now lists its empty properties by name instead of a column of rows that say Empty.
entries.detail: Choose one and it joins the list with its editor already open, and it stays there while the Page is open. Hidden properties that hold a value still open as rows.

entries.lead: The built-in Parent property is now called **Part of**, so a Page under another reads "Part of" followed by that Page.
entries.detail: A property you renamed keeps your name. Part of and Waits for also have their own icons.

entries.lead: Clicking an image in a Page's Files, or an image attachment in its body, now shows it over the Page instead of opening a tab.
entries.detail: Step through the Page's images with the arrow keys, and choose **Open in tab** when you want to keep one open; Cmd/Ctrl-click still opens the tab directly.

entries.lead: A Page's Files now hang beneath the Files property as an outline instead of sitting in a frame of their own.
entries.detail: Folders and Files are indented under the **Files** label, which folds and unfolds them, and pointing at a File adds Save and its menu beside its size. Files the Page body already shows start folded, and you can drop files from your computer onto the property to add them. Property icons also line up with the Page's title, and every value starts on one edge.

entries.lead: Images without a filename of their own get readable names.
entries.detail: A screenshot pasted from the clipboard is now called `Pasted image.png`, and other unnamed images `Image.png`, instead of a long identifier, in a Page's Files, the Library and chats. Images that come with a real filename keep it, and Files you already have keep their names.

entries.lead: Nodex tells you when a chat finishes while you are reading another one.
entries.detail: Turn completion notifications used to stay silent whenever a Nodex window was focused, so an Automation's run or a second chat could finish unnoticed. Now only the chat in front of you stays quiet by default. Settings offers this as **When the chat isn't in view**; choose **When Nodex is in the background** to keep banners away while a Nodex window is focused.

entries.lead: Heartbeat chats read like conversations.
entries.detail: A heartbeat's message shows its instructions and names the Automation that sent it, and the Agent's reply shows what it wrote, without the surrounding markup. Checks that found nothing to report fold into a single **Quiet check** line, and a run of them shares one line with their count and latest result; expand it to see any check in full.

entries.lead: Agents run `nodex` directly in their shells.
entries.detail: Nodex resolves who is asking each time the command runs, so a script an Agent wrote in an earlier turn keeps working after Nodex restarts, and its changes stay credited to the chat that made them. `nodex context` shows who the command is acting as and which Space and Project it targets, and a refused command says why and what to do next.

entries.lead: A retry key can be any text up to 128 characters, in chats and with `--idempotency-key`.
entries.detail: Reuse a key with the same request to retry a call whose result you did not see; Nodex remembers it for seven days.

entries.lead: Command line results are short.
entries.detail: A write reports what changed on each Page, with the values before and after, and leaves out internal detail.

entries.lead: Sending a message while an Agent is working in the Browser no longer makes it start over.
entries.detail: The message used to wipe the Agent's script session, so it lost its connection to the Browser and had to find its pages again. The session now stays as it was, and whatever the Agent was doing finishes first; Stop still ends it immediately.

entries.lead: An Agent reloading a page in the Browser no longer reloads all of Nodex.
entries.detail: The whole window used to start over, which interrupted the chat you were reading and closed every Browser tab, losing anything unsaved in them. Only the Agent's page reloads now.

entries.lead: Links that open a new tab work in the built-in Browser.
entries.detail: Clicking one did nothing, and neither did ⌘-click, middle-click or a page opening a window itself. They now open a tab right beside the page, in the background for ⌘-click and middle-click, including from a page you are not looking at. Mail and phone links that ask for a new tab open their app, and a tab opened only to download a file closes once the download finishes.

entries.lead: A page with unsaved changes asks before you leave it.
entries.detail: Following a link, reloading or entering another address did nothing on such a page; Nodex now asks **Leave site?**, and a page an Agent is working in moves on without asking.

entries.lead: The Browser stays idle with several tabs open.
entries.detail: With two or more live tabs Nodex re-sent their state many times a second, which used the processor continuously and could leave a new tab titled “Browser”. Background tabs now also show their page's title as soon as it loads.

entries.lead: Claude Code chats in Full access no longer stall on a safety check while you are away.
entries.detail: Claude Code still asks before a command whose removals it cannot verify, even a harmless script, and the request used to wait for you indefinitely. It now waits two minutes and shows that deadline; if no one answers, the command is declined, the Agent rewrites it safely or leaves the removal to you, and the turn carries on.

entries.lead: Starting a chat no longer fails with **Request declined** while Nodex is busy in the background.
entries.detail: Automatic work such as Inbox routing, scheduled work, and syncing now waits behind what you are doing, and a brief busy moment is retried instead of ending the turn.

entries.lead: Claude Code chats honor the selected model when an older version is turned off.
entries.detail: If Claude Code cannot apply the selection, the chat explains why the message was held. If Claude Code changes models during a reply, the chat names the model it used.

entries.lead: A follow-up sent to a delegated task while it is still working now wakes the Agent that sent it.
entries.detail: Before, a follow-up queued behind the task's unfinished work could complete without ever reporting back, and the reply named the task that had not run it. Each follow-up now gets its own task, and the task ID it returns is the one that reports the result.

entries.lead: Bash commands in Claude chats no longer stop with "still settling" after an earlier command was cut short.
entries.detail: Nodex no longer holds a command back to check which Run started its shell, so every command runs. A background command that outlives its Run is credited to the chat's current Run.

entries.lead: Linking a phone or inviting a Member works again on Spaces that have been in use for more than a week.
entries.detail: Creating a link, redeeming one, and changing Space or Member administration no longer fail with "legacy operation identity".

entries.lead: Local images load more reliably on Windows.
A new Windows host can start a team Space.
entries.detail: Nodex protects its settings encryption key with native Windows permissions when it creates the key.

entries.lead: A chat's composer no longer disappears.
entries.detail: Opening a chat that finished in the background could show its messages with nothing below them while it reconnected, after its connection failed, or after its worktree was cleaned up. The composer now stays with your draft, and a line above it says what is holding the next message and offers the fix, such as Retry or Restore worktree. A chat that failed to connect also tries again on its own when you come back to it.

entries.lead: Ended background tasks clear from the Session summary after you stop an Agent.
entries.detail: You can also use Stop to dismiss an already-ended task that still appears.

entries.lead: A heartbeat that has nothing to report stays quiet.
entries.detail: It no longer marks its chat unread or adds to unread Automation runs, matching the notification it already skipped. Automations set to notify on failed runs only keep their successful runs quiet the same way.

entries.lead: A Database no longer fails to open after a card moves into it.
entries.detail: Moving a card to another Database without choosing a column could leave it with no Status, and the receiving Database then showed an invalid workflow status error. A moved card now keeps its Status, Status can no longer be cleared, and cards already affected are repaired to Triage.

entries.lead: Editing a card's properties updates its last-edited time, so sorting and filtering by recent edits include cards whose Status or other properties changed.
`nodex page replace` rewrites long Pages in one step and keeps unchanged blocks, with their comments and links, in place.

`nodex page move --to page:ID` works as its help describes, a move prepared for one destination cannot be applied to another, and `nodex page rename` takes the Page first and points out swapped arguments.
Command line input errors name the field that is wrong and the values allowed there, and an unknown command suggests the one you likely meant.

releases.headline: Team Spaces and coordinated Agent work

entries.lead: Open and edit skills as pages.
entries.detail: Customize groups skills by folder and shows which Agents read each one. Open a skill from a chat or the command palette, edit its instructions with changes saved directly to disk, or duplicate a read-only skill to make your own copy.

entries.lead: Mention skills in Pages with `$` or the Skills section of `@`.
entries.detail: Click a mention to open the skill’s instructions. When you send the Page text to a chat, the mention becomes a skill invocation in the message.

entries.lead: Nodex now coordinates your chats.
entries.detail: One long-lived Nodex conversation routes every Inbox message knowing what is already running, watches the chats it starts, and keeps your Inbox focused on waiting messages and Pages waiting for you. Nodex adds a note when a Page needs more context, and one notification follows each episode. A chat can return a misrouted message with a reason for Nodex to route again. Reply to a Page waiting for you and your words go straight to its active chat, or answer the question it asked; open Nodex from the Inbox header to talk to it directly, and turn on Start my requests to let it start what you clearly ask for without a click. Work advances through Triage, Todo, In Progress and In Review as it starts and reports; your later Status choices take precedence. Accept reviewed work with `nodex page accept`; canceled work retires without releasing its dependents.

entries.lead: Pages have an Owner and one Assignee, either a person or an Agent.
entries.detail: Board cards can wait for one another, and an Agent Assignee can be set to Start automatically. Cards, List rows, the Inbox and each Page’s Status say plainly whose move a Page waits for, such as Needs your answer, Ready for Alice’s review, Codex is working, Queued · 2nd or Waiting for NODEX-2. A Page’s Status offers Start, Resume, Accept or Open chat when you can act, while your later Status choices take precedence. Start hands a card to a chat Nodex watches, a card set to Start automatically starts once the cards it waits for are done, and for a bigger request Nodex can propose a plan that creates and starts its cards in one step.

entries.lead: Each Page’s Agent work in a Git Project gets its own branch and worktree, shared by its later chats.
entries.detail: A new chat opens with its prompt while Nodex prepares the checkout. If preparation fails, the chat shows the reason and lets you retry. The Page shows its pull request and the GitHub threads it follows, the Board shows its pull request, and completing or canceling the Page removes the idle checkout while keeping the branch and PR link.

entries.lead: Work that starts without you, such as Automations and Pages set to start automatically, waits behind a limit you choose in Agents settings, initially four, and shows its place in the queue.
entries.detail: Your own chats and the tasks they delegate never wait.

entries.lead: Pause Agent work for a Page, a Project, or the whole Space.
entries.detail: Running work stops while queued messages and results wait for you to resume, including across restarts.

entries.lead: Your Agents can do what you can in Nodex.
entries.detail: Ask a chat to start, pause, resume or accept work, set a card to Start automatically, set up an Automation that runs on its own or start one waiting for you in the Inbox, and History and Activity show it acted on your behalf. By default it asks before unattended work, leaves its own work for your review and leaves work you paused alone.

entries.lead: Watch GitHub from Settings → GitHub.
entries.detail: Choose repositories and discover assignments, review requests and mentions. Updates on followed threads reach the Page's active chat, verified PR milestones move its stage, and new GitHub requests arrive in the Inbox for your decision. Nodex can acknowledge a request and post its result back to its GitHub origin. Problems in the Inbox offer a fix, and Activity explains routing, milestones, delivery and recovery. Polling, delivery and replies resume safely after restart.

entries.lead: Work with other people in a team Space.
entries.detail: Join one from the account menu at the bottom of the rail, then switch between Spaces there or from the command palette, moving between a team's Pages, Boards and Inbox alongside your personal Space; each Space keeps its own layout, and losing access to a team leaves personal work untouched. Settings → Spaces shows who is in the Space and which devices reach it: Owners invite people, revoke Devices, remove Members and rename the Space, and everyone links and revokes their own Devices. Remote access lets your phone and other computers reach your personal Space without sharing it. Connections pin the host's certificate and resume live after a dropped network. History records who made each change, and each person keeps their own Inbox, unread chats, pins, reminders and View preferences across devices.

entries.lead: Run a team Space on an always-on machine with `nodex serve`.
entries.detail: It initializes the Space, its Owner and certificate, runs Agents, Sources and Automations without desktop windows, and keeps working while everyone's laptops are closed. Members start chats and work on the host from their desktops and phones and use hosted chats as they would their own: attach images, files and Pages, fork, open side chats and edit their last message. The person who started a chat and the Space's Owners rename, archive, compact or stop it, and questions and approvals stay with the Member entitled to answer them. Host status reports when Agents share the host account's file access.

entries.lead: Claude Fable 5.2 is available, and new Claude models appear as soon as your Claude Code offers them.
entries.detail: Claude chats list the models your installed Claude Code offers your account, with their effort, Fast and Ultracode choices, without waiting for a Nodex update. The default Fable model and the name `fable` follow the Fable model Claude Code gives you; Fable 5.2 needs Claude Code 2.1.321 or newer.

entries.lead: See how an agent understood your request without going back to its chat.
entries.detail: When you send a message and move on, the agent's opening statement, what it says it will do before it starts, appears briefly at the top of the window you are in. Point at it to read all of it, Stop the agent or Reply to correct it on the spot, or click it to open the chat. A working chat's hover card in the sidebar shows the same statement. Turn it off in Settings → General → Notifications.

entries.lead: The Page open beside a chat is no longer sent with every message.
entries.detail: The Composer shows it as a dashed suggestion; click it to send a link to that Page, and the Blocks you selected, with your next message, and click again to take it back. Each new message starts without it.

entries.lead: A chat without a Project now has a folder of its own from the start.
entries.detail: Open a Terminal or Files in a new chat before sending anything, and the first message runs in that same folder. The project menu shows where the chat will work and lets you choose an existing folder instead; new folders live under `Chats` in your Nodex folder and are named after non-English prompts too. Once started, the chat's summary shows its folder, and Turn into project makes that folder a Project without moving anything. Deleting a chat removes its folder only when Nodex created it and it is still empty.

entries.lead: Agents hear from the tasks they delegate while they keep working.
entries.detail: A delegated task's question or result reaches its Agent at the next pause between tools instead of after its whole reply, and Claude Code no longer stops its running tools to take one in. Waiting on one task also returns for another task's question, and answering a task that already finished says plainly that it starts follow-up work. A question the Agent leaves unanswered is handed to you.

entries.lead: The Inbox's History is now part of Activity, one timeline of everything handled in that Inbox.
entries.detail: Each message you send to a chat, file, keep or finish is a single line beside what Nodex, your Automations and GitHub did, and All, Messages, Nodex & automations and Problems narrow it down. Expand a message's line to read it, see why it went where it did, and open its chat, return it to the Inbox, mark it done or delete it. A chat it went to shows its live state on the line while the work is under way.

entries.lead: Scheduled tasks are now Automations.
entries.detail: Keep the same schedules, runbooks, waiting Inbox runs and history, and choose Dry run, Ask first or Run; only an Automation’s Owner, or an Agent working for them, can let it run on its own. Automations can also react to GitHub events: a dry run records each judgement and its reason, Ask first proposes work in the Owner’s Inbox, and Run starts Pages under a standing grant.

entries.lead: Nodex Mobile now links to each of your Spaces as one of your Devices, team Spaces included.
entries.detail: Scan the code from Settings → Spaces → Link a device, switch between linked Spaces on the phone, and keep working in a team Space while its host runs, even with your laptop closed. Capture to your personal or team Inbox, start chats, answer your Page’s questions, accept reviewed work and follow chats live with every picture in them. Each Space is reachable at its local, Tailscale or DNS address over a connection pinned to that Space’s certificate, and on iPhone it tells you only about what is yours to answer, while you're away from your computer. Removing the phone’s Device ends its access immediately. Settings > Mobile is gone; link a phone you paired before again from Settings → Spaces.

entries.lead: Nodex Mobile has a menu for where you're looking.
entries.detail: Tap the Space's avatar, or swipe right across the Inbox, to choose the Library's Inbox or any Project's, see how many messages wait in each, and switch to another linked Space. Choosing an Inbox no longer means opening the Composer first, each Space remembers the one you chose, and the Composer says which Project a thought will go to.

entries.lead: Side chats now stay with the chat they came from.
entries.detail: Closing a side chat's tab, quitting or restarting no longer discards it: its tab comes back where you left it after a restart, a closed side chat reopens from the chat's summary, and `Delete side chat` in its tab menu removes it for good. Closing a side chat no longer asks for confirmation. Side chats of remote conversations remain temporary.

entries.lead: Side chat tabs and tool tabs such as Plan, Automation, Subagents and process output can be dragged like any other tab.
entries.detail: Reorder them, move them to another tab group or the bottom panel, or drop them on a group's edge to split it; tool tabs stay in the right panel.

entries.lead: Clicking a file attached in a Page now opens it, instead of a small details popup.
entries.detail: A file saved in the Page opens in a tab beside the Page, just like from the Page's Files list, so Markdown renders, HTML reports show as pages, and images, PDFs and media play. A linked file opens in Files. Right-click a file for Open in new tab, Save… and Copy reference, and press Enter on a selected file to open it. In Page history and other read-only previews, a file opens in a viewer that shows the version that was captured.

entries.lead: Save as chat is gone from side chats, which now keep their conversation on their own.
On iOS 27, tapping a button in Nodex Mobile's top bar no longer also scrolls the list beneath it to the top.
entries.detail: Opening Settings used to leave the Inbox at its oldest message.

entries.lead: Older chats open again after upgrading Nodex.
Dropping a tab on the edge of a tab group now splits the group instead of doing nothing.
Page history opens again after you edit a Page and pause.
entries.detail: The automatic revision Nodex saves when you stop editing made the Page's history show a database error instead of its revisions.

entries.lead: Usage analytics that is off when Nodex starts no longer sends events an earlier launch left waiting.
entries.detail: Setting `DO_NOT_TRACK`, or otherwise turning analytics off while Nodex was closed, now discards them as turning it off in Settings does.

entries.lead: Agent settings edits through symbolic links apply reliably, including immediately after startup or after a link points to a new file.
A heartbeat's unread dot in Automations clears once you open its chat.
entries.detail: It used to stay forever, because only a cron run opened from its folder was marked read. Any finished run is now read as soon as its chat is on screen, however you got there.

entries.lead: Heartbeats run on their schedule.
entries.detail: An hourly heartbeat ran about every 90 minutes, and one set to every few minutes waited half an hour between runs, because Nodex postponed each one after its own previous run. A heartbeat now waits only while its chat is busy, and counts its interval from when the previous run started, so a long run no longer pushes the next one back. Heartbeats an hour or more apart start within five minutes either side of their time.

entries.lead: Every Agent can now set up and change Automations, reorder Sidebar Sections and manage a chat's queued messages, not only Codex.
entries.detail: Claude Code never saw these Nodex tools, and its heartbeats now stay quiet unless something needs you.

entries.lead: Browser tools that sit over a web page show again.
entries.detail: The annotation composer, the device toolbar's resize handles and the offer to save a password were hidden behind the page, as was the sidebar when it slid over a full-width Browser.

releases.headline: Nodex Mobile beta and a Dock badge

entries.lead: Nodex's Dock icon now shows how many chats are unread.
entries.detail: It counts the same chats the sidebar marks unread across every Project, updates as soon as you read one anywhere, including on your phone, and clears when Nodex closes. Turn it off with Badges in Nodex's notification settings in System Settings.

entries.lead: Get Nodex Mobile from its public TestFlight beta on iPhone, or download the Android app from nodex.jyu.app/download.
entries.detail: Every Nodex release now ships the phone app with the same version, so the phone and the computer it pairs with stay able to talk; TestFlight keeps the iPhone app current, and a newer APK installs over the old one without losing your pairing.

entries.lead: Each Nodex window is now named after what it shows, so you can tell windows apart in the Window menu, Mission Control, the Dock and window switchers.
entries.detail: A chat window shows the chat and its Project, such as `Fix flaky E2E — nodex`; a Project, Page or Database window shows its name; and titles follow renames and Page title edits as they happen. On Windows the title ends with Nodex.

entries.lead: Nodex Mobile clears notifications for chats you've already read on your computer.
entries.detail: As soon as the app connects, and whenever your chats change while it's open, notifications for chats that are read, archived or gone from your chat list leave Notification Center.

entries.lead: Your phone now hears from Nodex only when you're away from your computer.
entries.detail: A chat you're watching on the desktop no longer buzzes your phone. The phone is told at once when the computer's screen is locked or nobody has used it for five minutes, and otherwise only if you walk away before touching the computer again. Answering, opening the chat anywhere, or a newer notification in the same chat withdraws one that is still waiting. A chat open on your phone no longer raises a desktop notification or turns unread, and opening it there clears its desktop notifications. A locked screen counts as out of sight on the desktop too, so chats that finish while it is locked turn unread and notify as usual. Chat reminders now reach your phone as well.

entries.lead: Folders in the Files tree collapse again when a folder inside them is open.
entries.detail: Previously the open folder inside kept reopening its parent; now it keeps its own state and is open again when you reopen the parent. Large folders also show a loading row until their entries arrive, and scrolling long folders no longer slows the Files panel.

entries.lead: Your phone no longer says a chat finished while it is about to continue with a queued message or delegated results, and no longer sends a finish and a question for the same moment.
entries.detail: Phone notifications now follow exactly the same rules as desktop notifications.

releases.headline: Mobile apps, Insights and quick setup

entries.lead: A new Profile now opens on a short setup instead of a sample Project.
entries.detail: It shows which Agents Nodex found, lets you sign in or install the ones you want, or add Nodex credits if you'd rather pay as you go, offers the projects you've already used with Codex and Claude Code, and lands on New Chat with a first task ready to send. Nothing is created until you choose it, and `Run setup again` in Settings replays it.

entries.lead: Insights shows what your agents did across this device, and turns it into a card you can share.
entries.detail: Open it from the rail to see tokens, models, cost at API list price, messages, how many agents ran at once, tasks finished and Pages written, including Claude Code and Codex history from before you installed Nodex. Reading that history takes one click to allow and keeps only counts on your device. Share makes a Skyline or Receipt image to copy, save or post, with no project names or prompts on it.

entries.lead: Archiving a chat now lets you take it back.
entries.detail: A toast appears right away: Undo restores the chat and returns you to it, and View opens your archived chats.

entries.lead: Settings now shows exactly what usage analytics send.
entries.detail: Open See what is sent in Settings → General → Privacy to read your random ID and every event waiting or sent since launch. Prompts, code, titles and file paths have no field to travel in.

entries.lead: The Codex usage ring now shows your remaining credits.
entries.detail: Hover it to see your balance below the usage windows. When a limit is used up and credits keep you working, the ring turns amber instead of red, and the card says the credits are in use.

entries.lead: You choose which models Nodex can use in Settings → Models.
entries.detail: An off model leaves every model menu, and nothing in Nodex can start it. Nodex credits are protected by default: only what you start can spend them, so an Agent on another provider can't start a Nodex subagent unless you allow it, and turning Nodex off means nothing on this computer can spend them.

entries.lead: Account settings now show what each Nodex model costs.
entries.detail: Model prices lists input, cache and output prices per million tokens in credits, always current with what the service charges, so you can see what a top-up buys before you pay.

entries.lead: You can add and remove images when you edit a sent message.
entries.detail: Its images move into the editor, where you can paste, drop or pick more and remove any of them, so a wrong screenshot no longer means starting over. An image whose file was lost shows as failed, and removing it lets the edit through.

entries.lead: Every Agent can now use the built-in Browser, your Chrome, and Computer Use:
entries.detail: Claude Code, OpenCode, and ACP agents such as Gemini CLI, as well as Codex. Ask one to open a page, test your local app, or work in a Mac app, and Nodex asks before it runs code or reaches a new site or app. Type `$` in the composer to pick one of these skills yourself, and on macOS the chat summary can show what the Agent is doing in picture in picture.

entries.lead: Nodex now has an iOS and Android app.
entries.detail: Drop a thought into the Inbox, start a chat, follow a running chat live, and answer its approvals and questions from your phone. Turn it on and pair a phone in Settings > Mobile. It connects directly to your computer over your local network or a tailnet, encrypted end to end, and captures made offline send when your computer is back.

entries.lead: You can stop an Inbox suggestion that is taking too long.
entries.detail: Hover its spinner and click stop: the work ends at once, no more usage is spent, and the message keeps any advice it had or offers Suggest.

entries.lead: You choose the reasoning effort and speed Inbox suggestions run at, in the same model menu new chats use.
entries.detail: Until you do, they stay at high on Codex and medium on Claude.

entries.lead: You choose which model titles your chats in Settings → General.
entries.detail: Until you pick one, a light model on the chat's own Agent writes the title, such as GPT-6 Luna on Codex and Haiku on Claude Code, so titles cost less on your expensive models. A model you pick receives each chat's first message, and can also title chats on Agents that can't generate text themselves.

entries.lead: A Terminal's tab names the program running in it.
entries.detail: The title a program sets replaces the folder name while it runs, unless it only repeats the working directory.

entries.lead: Agent activity now says what happened in plain language, naming the Pages and chats it touched instead of showing IDs.
entries.detail: Rows read like `Read Launch plan` or `Updated Launch plan +2 -1`, every Nodex tool has one, and clicking a name opens that Page or chat. Opening a row shows the result for reading, such as the formatted Page or the diff, and hovering a Nodex or MCP tool row reveals an inspector with the exact input, output and record.

entries.lead: OpenCode models now start off, free ones included, so a new chat never lands on a third party's model unless you chose it.
entries.detail: Turn them on during setup or in Settings → Models.

entries.lead: You can now search the conversations you import from Codex and Claude Code.
entries.detail: Settings → Conversations lists your whole history as soon as it opens: type to find a conversation by title or folder, filter by Agent, folder or import status, and select across several searches before importing. The same field still takes a pasted link or ID, and the list and its import controls now stay on screen together however long your history is.

entries.lead: New chats remember the model you last chose for one, on any Agent.
entries.detail: Pick Claude Code, OpenCode or a Nodex model in a new chat and the next one starts there with the same effort and options, instead of going back to Codex. Switching models inside a chat you already started now stays with that chat, so it no longer changes what new chats start on.

entries.lead: Notifications stack at the top of the window.
entries.detail: Up to three show at once and fan out when you hover them, hovering pauses their timers, and you can swipe one away.

entries.lead: Usage analytics and crash reports are now on by default, and first launch says so.
entries.detail: Nothing is sent until you have had a minute to turn it off in Settings → General → Privacy, and turning usage analytics off takes effect at once and discards anything unsent. `DO_NOT_TRACK` is respected. Session replays stay off unless you enable them, and the separate web analytics setting is gone because Nodex no longer collects web analytics in the app.

entries.lead: Reviewing unsaved edits now shows exactly what they would add to the Page.
entries.detail: Word-level changes appear in place, unchanged content folds away, and one sentence says what restoring does or that nothing was lost, so you no longer compare two full copies by eye. Edits that can't be merged can still be copied back with one click, and discarding applies immediately with Undo.

entries.lead: Agent chats now take far less disk space, and their history no longer grows without limit.
entries.detail: A store of about 9 GB from a month of heavy use shrank to about 2.5 GB. Nodex keeps a day or two of internal activity instead of all of it, compresses command output, and no longer records hooks that finish with nothing to report. An older store upgrades once, which can pause the first Agent start after updating and a later one for a few minutes. History keeps the first and last 128 KiB of a command's output, and Hooks now appears on a reply only when a hook failed, blocked, stopped or reported something.

entries.lead: Nodex prepaid balances are now counted in credits instead of dollars, at 25 credits to $1.
entries.detail: Your balance keeps its value and reads as a whole number, and Top up shows how many credits each amount adds.

entries.lead: The macOS installer is about 30% smaller, so first-time downloads finish sooner, and Nodex uses about 250 MB less disk space.
entries.detail: Opening the disk image and copying Nodex to Applications take a little longer on a first install.

entries.lead: The Windows installer is about a fifth smaller, and installing it takes less disk space.
Full macOS updates are about 40% smaller, so updating downloads much less when an incremental update isn't available.
Inbox suggestions no longer wait in line behind each other.
entries.detail: Up to five run at once, or as many as 16 if you raise the limit in Settings → Inbox, so a message that takes a while to look into doesn't hold up the ones after it, and every message waiting for advice shows its own spinner instead of only the newest one.

entries.lead: `⌘K` (`Ctrl+K` on Windows and Linux) clears a focused Terminal.
entries.detail: It opens the command palette everywhere else.

entries.lead: Agents now show the HTML pages they make as rendered pages beside the chat.
entries.detail: Opening one used to show its source code. An Agent opening the page again reloads the same tab, so you see its edits, and it can still show you the source when you ask.

entries.lead: A chat that continues after a restart can open tabs beside it again.
entries.detail: With several windows open, its Agent used to stop and show you nothing; it now uses the window showing that chat.

entries.lead: The marker showing that a chat moved to another Agent now stays visible.
entries.detail: It says which Agents the chat moved between and what it carried, and it used to fold away as soon as the reply finished.

entries.lead: Returning a chat to Codex keeps Codex's own conversation.
entries.detail: A resume that had already succeeded could be thrown away because its background terminals couldn't be listed, which started a new conversation and pasted the whole history into it.

entries.lead: Fast mode now works on current Codex models.
entries.detail: The Fast toggle, `/fast`, the speed setting for new chats, a scheduled task's speed and `speed="fast"` in a prompt's agent config had no effect or failed, because these models name the tier differently. If you turned Fast on earlier, new chats now really run at Fast and use more of your usage; turn it off in the model menu or Settings.

entries.lead: Claude Code chats no longer stop partway through a long tool call.
entries.detail: A long script or file could end the reply and kill the command it was running; how much an Agent streams can no longer end a reply.

entries.lead: Chats woken by finished background work no longer end silently after an error.
entries.detail: If the Agent stopped during that reply, the chat looked finished until you typed “continue”; now it recovers and carries on like any other reply, on Claude Code, OpenCode and ACP Agents.

entries.lead: Long chats no longer use more memory the longer an Agent runs.
entries.detail: A Turn with thousands of messages or file changes now holds only its most recent work in memory, even while it runs and when you are looking elsewhere, and earlier work loads back as you scroll up.

entries.lead: Settings → Data controls now lists every archived chat.
entries.detail: Most archived chats used to be missing from it, so they couldn't be found or restored there, and restoring some of the ones it did list failed.

entries.lead: Searching your chats and reading one from another Agent now shows only what you wrote.
